newsitem.title: CHINA: China opens lantern festival to mark HK return.
newsitem.headline: China opens lantern festival to mark HK return.

text.p: China switched on the lights on Sunday in a huge cardboard model of Hong Kong built in the grounds of a former imperial summer palace that was burned down by British and French troops in the 19th century.
"Very few people in China have been to Hong Kong and Hong Kong is returning to China very soon," Liu Yuxiu, director of the tourism administration of Beijing's Haidian district, told Reuters.

"So in this park we have set up this spectacle of Hong Kong for people who want to see what Hong Kong looks like," he said, gesturing toward the bright, neon-lit skyline of the model city built on a small lake in the Yuanmingyuan park.

China resumes sovereignty over Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of British colonial rule that Beijing and many of China's 1.2 billion people regard as a century and a half of national shame.
"The Yuanmingyuan is one of the national humiliations of China... but we will recover Hong Kong very soon and the recovery of Hong Kong will wash away these 100 years of shame," Liu said.

The huge model of Hong Kong in miniature, complete with celebratory neon fireworks lighting up the sky above, stands on the site of a magnificent palace, summer retreat of Beijing's emperors, that British and French troops looted and destroyed in 1860.
After that defeat, China was forced to pay an indemnity to the invaders as well as to hand over to Britain the Kowloon Peninsula, part of the modern-day territory of Hong Kong.

It was one of a series of "unequal treaties" imposed during the 19th century opium wars as London tried to prise open China's markets. Beijing was obliged to cede Hong Kong island and other districts, and to lease to Britain an adjoining area which became known as the New Territories.
"This lantern festival is part of our welcome from the city of Beijing to the return of Hong Kong," Liu said.
Hundreds of sightseers crowded into the park for what may be their closest glimpse of the territory.

China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong in just 23 days will not make it any easier for Chinese to obtain permission to enter the territory since its system is to remain unchanged for 50 years in line with Sino-British treaties governing the handover.
"I hope one day to be able to see the real Hong Kong," said one student from a nearby university as he gazed across the lake at the model of Hong Kong.
